$comment: Invariant ids that MUST have an owning test right now. `pnpm test:coverage-map` fails when an id listed here has no test whose name contains it. The registry itself lives in docs/invariants.md and carries 424 ids; this file says which of them are load-bearing today. From P1 on, each task also files docs/owned/<task>.json and the coverage map reads the UNION; an id must appear in exactly one of those files.
phaseNote: P0 owns the ids below (plan §Phases, P0 gate: DAY-01/05 + CER-01 at 10,000 cases in four zones, the PER-06 DB-path gate, and the PLAT-01/02 build gates). P1 extends this list with every id in §1-§10 (SESS, GRD, SCH, ECO, PATH, DAY, FRZ/REC, CER), §13 (PER/DAT) and §14 (PACK/AUD) engine parts, plus SEC-01/02 — see the plan's P1 gate row, and docs/owned/*.json for the per-task split. Adding an id here without its test turns CI red, which is the point: an invariant with no owning test is worse than a failing one.
cer01Note: INV-CER-01 was P0's and moved to docs/owned/ceremony.json at P1 integration. It is not listed twice: `phase-roster.test.ts` fails on an id claimed by two ownership files, and the ceremony lane now owns the invariant, its tests and its falsifying input. Ownership moving between phases is normal; being claimed twice is not.
